title: s(127), s(204), s(232), s(264), s(305): lowered upper bounds on Tomáš Kodaj's public packings: registration request
body:
**Credit name.** JoeGun ([@JonathanGun](https://github.com/JonathanGun)). Each packing below is a public Kaggle packing by Tomáš Kodaj ([tomkodaj](https://www.kaggle.com/tomkodaj)) that we improved further. Please credit him as the finder.

**Claim.** Five upper bounds. Each side is the witness's exact rational side, rounded up at 12 places. The record column is `packing/witnesses/known-best` at `31ddae6`.

| n | claimed side | record now | lower by | Kodaj's public side | our part |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 127 | 11.801753890487 | 11.8108787875891799 | 9.1249e-3 | 11.801765635430 | 1.174e-5 |
| 204 | 14.802646843107 | 14.8043613836518588 | 1.7145e-3 | 14.802646907234 | 6.41e-8 |
| 232 | 15.759531627557 | 15.7614096448817244 | 1.8780e-3 | 15.759531732104 | 1.045e-7 |
| 264 | 16.773807598002 | 16.7747351323878329 | 9.275e-4 | 16.773891500852 | 8.390e-5 |
| 305 | 17.945762359659 | 17.9504664821377123 | 4.7041e-3 | 17.946298110350 | 5.358e-4 |

"Our part" is Kodaj's side minus ours. The rest of each gain is his. These are upper bounds only. We make no optimality, rigidity or KKT claim.

**Certificate.** Five `Witness/v2` files with rational corners, `n-NNN-candidate.yaml`, in https://github.com/JonathanGun/square-packing-upper-bounds at commit `bc10ce471c9d7841b9a53b383dae87d23dbe5a99`. The f64 pose behind each one is `n-NNN-decimal-pose.yaml` in the same commit.

```
9bde48b76afce9ab7d20d6d180650d0a6bbe46b7f106573f8155dfe9ed9d06f0  n-127-candidate.yaml
1daa0e09b5b403e4e47048104c760f3d8a9b6997d77d26a30930bf1e257ea90c  n-204-candidate.yaml
93d856c25c9f75842ca5e36552ccb726e87884440689c9ce4100d2a58d5a279d  n-232-candidate.yaml
14fef8f163b2cdb9062f714cdd41d81dce2447691a2de55e3797810cdcd676ee  n-264-candidate.yaml
14d2e37e22218defb238e0b0e657f139bab0c2873cc3d05f781b0f3b13a75494  n-305-candidate.yaml
```

The exact coordinates come from this repository's `packing-witness promote --strategy robust-rational --max-side-increase 1e-11` at `31ddae6`. It reports `center_dilation: '1'` and 36 rational digits for all five. Before promotion, our export pushes every centre away from the centroid by a factor of at least 1 + 1e-12.

**Checking.**
- `packing-witness verify` (jlevy/squares `main` at `31ddae6`, code unchanged): `VERIFIED` for all five, method exact-algebraic. Pairs tested: 8,001, 20,706, 26,796, 34,716 and 46,360. Output is in `packing-witness-verify.txt`.
- `check.py` (in the repository, written apart from the registry's code): `VALID` for all five. It uses `Fraction` arithmetic with no tolerance and no distance filter. Output is in `check-output.txt`. All five take about 30 seconds on a laptop.
- `check.py` refused three broken copies of the n = 127 witness:
  - the side lowered by 1e-30
  - square 2 placed on square 1
  - one corner moved by 1e-30
- Each exact side minus the record's exact side is negative in `Fraction` arithmetic.
- Rerun commands are in the README.

**What the checkers share.** The definitions (unit square, box, disjoint interiors) and the YAML file. The promotion used your tool. Therefore `packing-witness verify` does not check the rounding independently, and `check.py` does. We ran `packing-witness` from a sparse checkout of `31ddae6`. The README lists what it held.

**Not done.**
- No local-optimality, rigidity or KKT analysis.
- No proof-assistant check and no human review outside this project.
- No measurement of the least pair margin or of the contraction margin.
- The licence of Kodaj's notebook was not checked.
- We found no open issue or pull request here for these five counts below the record (checked `31ddae6`, 2026-11-16).

**Lineage and credit.**
- Tomáš Kodaj published all five parent packings in his Kaggle notebook [Squares in Squares | [22.1636]](https://www.kaggle.com/code/tomkodaj/squares-in-squares-22-1636). Its last run was 2026-11-13 09:48 UTC. We downloaded it at 10:17 UTC that day. We did not trace what his packings build on.
- Our steps on top of his packings:

| n | step | when (UTC) | side after |
|---|---|---|---|
| 127 | fault-line DP | 2026-11-13 10:42 | 11.80175389 |
| 204 | fault-line DP | 2026-11-13 10:42 | 14.80264684 |
| 232 | fault-line DP | 2026-11-13 10:42 | 15.75953163 |
| 264 | quench, 600 s | 2026-11-14 09:42 | 16.77380760 |
| 305 | quench, two runs | 2026-11-13 13:41 | 17.94578855 |
| 305 | fault-line DP | 2026-11-13 23:40 | 17.94576236 |

- Fault-line DP is our own method. It cuts pieces out of other packings along lines that no square crosses. A dynamic programme then joins the pieces into a packing of the wanted count. The donor packings are our own and public Kaggle ones. We did not record which donors the winning pieces came from.
- The quench is Evan Daniel's code from [evand/square-packing](https://github.com/evand/square-packing) (MIT, at `6067db5`).
- Suggested credit: Tomáš Kodaj as finder at all five counts, improved by JoeGun, and the quench to Evan Daniel. At 204 and 232 our part is below 2e-7, so credit to Kodaj alone is fair there.

**Licence.** The repository has `LICENSE.md`: CC BY 4.0 for the witnesses, poses, outputs and text, MIT for `check.py`. It covers our own contribution and does not change the terms of Kodaj's work. Evan Daniel's MIT notice is in `LICENSE-evand-square-packing.txt`.

**Other public values.** The Kaggle per-puzzle leaderboard (read 2026-11-16 04:38 UTC) lists side-only entries below ours at all five counts. They state no packing, so we could not check them.

| n | leaderboard side | team |
|---|---|---|
| 127 | 11.800793726617 | nubx |
| 204 | 14.802436041464 | Luka Cvetkovic |
| 232 | 15.758852775266 | Robson |
| 264 | 16.770127228405 | Shadoks |
| 305 | 17.945755838742 | Shadoks |

Kodaj's notebook also holds n = 270 at 16.927469594094, below the record's 16.928148603343. We did not improve it, so it is not claimed here.

**AI assistance.** AI agents wrote and ran the search code, the checker and this filing. JoeGun directed the work.
